$comment: Inputs of `npm run assets:optimize`. Originals are never modified; optimized copies go to `optimized/<source path>` and the game picks them up through src/core/assets/assetRegistry.ts. See docs/PERFORMANCE_ARCHITECTURE.md.

character.$comment: Skinned cooks and robots. Bones, hair chains and node names are read by code (hairPhysics, armPose), so the hierarchy is untouched and positions stay float: only textures shrink. The cooks are ~100 px tall in the kitchen and at most ~half the screen in the menu.

animation.$comment: Clip packs: only their animations are used (retargeted by bone name). No meshopt: its quantization splits the pack's one shared skin into one skin per mesh (6 skeletons in Babylon), which the validation rejects. Measured 2026-10-15.

staticProp.$comment: Props that never animate internally and are never looked up by node name: parts sharing a material are joined into one mesh (fewer draw calls), geometry is meshopt-compressed.

prop.$comment: Moving props whose node structure is kept (disasters).

staticScene.$comment: Backdrops and dioramas. Node names are read (the level map places its stars on named landmarks), so no flatten/join.

images.$comment: Standalone images (CSS backgrounds, UI art): re-encoded to WebP and kept only when the result measures at least minPsnrDb against the original. Referenced from CSS by their optimized path, so Vite hashes them.
